title: Space-valued transport classification with its mapping-space comparison
statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small and all categories under discussion fit in $\mathcal U'$. Use the simplicial sets, spaces, quasicategories, coherent functors and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A left fibration is a simplicial map having the right lifting property against $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i<n$; a right fibration uses $0<i\leq n$. Write $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ for the infinity category presented by $\mathcal U$-small Kan complexes and their simplicial mapping complexes. For a $\mathcal U'$-small simplicial set $A$, space-valued transport gives an equivalence between $\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$ and the infinity category of left fibrations over $A$ with essentially $\mathcal U$-small fibers. A representative $q_F:E_F\to A$ for a functor $F$ has fiber equivalent to $F(a)$ at every vertex $a$. For two such representatives there is an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})}(F,G)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{/A}(E_F,E_G),$$
where the right side has $n$-simplices the maps $E_F\times\Delta^n\to E_G$ whose composite with $q_G$ is $q_F$ on the first factor. This simplicial set is Kan. The comparison is coherent in both functors and compatible with composition and pullback along maps of base simplicial sets. A constant functor with value $X$ corresponds to $A\times X\to A$. If $A$ is $\mathcal U$-small, the representatives can be chosen $\mathcal U$-small. There is the dual equivalence between $\operatorname{Fun}(A^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$ and right fibrations over $A$, with the same mapping-space formula.

For a locally $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory $\mathcal E$ in $\mathcal U'$, transport also supplies the coherent mapping bifunctor $H_{\mathcal E}:\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal E\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ with values naturally equivalent to the mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a vertex $e$, its restrictions $H_{\mathcal E}(-,e)$ and $H_{\mathcal E}(e,-)$ classify respectively the target-fixed arrow right fibration and the source-fixed arrow left fibration, whose total simplicial sets are $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal E)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,\mathcal E}\{e\}$ and $\{e\}\times_{\mathcal E,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal E)$. Under the arrow-to-join-slice comparison the former also classifies $\mathcal E_{/e}\to\mathcal E$, whose $n$-simplices are maps $\Delta^{n+1}\to\mathcal E$ with final vertex $e$ and whose projection restricts to the initial face. These identifications are coherent in $e$ and take the identity arrow to the identity element in $H_{\mathcal E}(e,e)$. Under these mapping-space identifications, transport in the first variable acts by precomposition and transport in the second variable acts by postcomposition, compatibly with the coherent composition and unit homotopies. In particular, an edge $v:e\to e'$ induces on the fiber at $x$ the map $a\mapsto v\circ a$ from $H_{\mathcal E}(x,e)$ to $H_{\mathcal E}(x,e')$, including its action on all higher simplices.

source.place: HTT Theorem 2.2.1.2 (contravariant straightening, printed p.74) and its covariant dual, together with Proposition 4.2.4.4 (coherent diagram comparison, printed p.258), for the full coherent classification. Kerodon Notation 7.4.2.1 and Theorem 7.4.2.4 with Remark 7.4.2.5 (05R5) specify the locally Kan fibration model and distinguish its homotopy-category comparison from the full upgrade. Kerodon Proposition 8.3.3.2 (03N2), Proposition 8.3.5.5 (03NK), and Subsection 5.6.6 (02HU) give the Hom-functor and identity/representable compatibilities. Read online, not archived in literature/. No matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: Work first in a universe $\mathcal V$ containing the base and all total spaces in question. The presentation [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] gives the ordinary Quillen equivalence with right adjoint $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_A F=(U_{A^{\mathrm{op}}}F)^{\mathrm{op}}$ from covariant strict diagrams to the covariant slice model category. Apply [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] to obtain the derived adjunction. Its unit on a cofibrant slice object $X$ is a weak equivalence: apply the Quillen-equivalence criterion to the weak equivalence $TX\to R(TX)$. Its counit on a fibrant diagram $F$ is a weak equivalence: apply the same criterion to $TQ(UF)\to F$, whose adjoint is the cofibrant replacement $Q(UF)\to UF$. These unit and counit transformations are therefore pointwise equivalences after localization, and hence equivalences by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Thus the derived adjunction is an equivalence. All slice objects are cofibrant and its fibrant objects are the left fibrations. By [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] its localization is consequently the coherent nerve of the locally Kan simplicial category $\mathsf{LFib}(A)$ with the usual mapping complexes. Apply [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification] with $K=A$, $\mathcal C=\mathfrak C[A]$, $u=1$, and $\mathcal M=\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V}$; the Kan model structure is combinatorial and simplicial by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]. It identifies the strict diagram localization with $\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$. Composing gives the left-fibration classification. On a cofibrant-fibrant strict diagram $F$ its representative is $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_AF$. Its fiber is naturally equivalent as a space to $F(a)$, by the presentation's fiber clause and rectification's evaluation clause. This argument uses the derived ordinary adjunction, with no claim that taking opposites is a simplicial functor for the usual mapping complexes.

source.place: Propositions 2.1.4.7–8 and Remark 2.1.4.12 (covariant/contravariant simplicial model structures), Theorem 2.2.1.2 (ordinary Quillen equivalence), and Proposition 4.2.4.4 (rectification); derived adjunction via the cited model-infinity-derived-adjunction node.

proof.text: The covariant slice model category of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] has all objects cofibrant and left fibrations fibrant. The mapping-space assertion of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] therefore identifies its localized mapping space between $E_F$ and $E_G$ with the actual simplicial set $\operatorname{Fun}_{/A}(E_F,E_G)$. In degree $n$ this consists precisely of maps $E_F\times\Delta^n\to E_G$ over $A$. It is Kan by the presentation, for every source over $A$ and a left-fibration target, without a quasicategory hypothesis on $A$. The functor-equivalence mapping-space clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], applied to the equivalence in step 1, gives the displayed comparison of spaces. Enriched composition over $A$ is ordinary composition with the shared $\Delta^n$ parameter: send $(g,f)$ to $(z,t)\mapsto g(f(z,t),t)$. This is associative and unital in each degree and commutes with every simplex operator. The localization mapping comparison respects these compositions by its stated clause. This gives coherence in both variables and compatibility with composition.

For $u:B\to A$ and a cofibrant-fibrant strict diagram $F:\mathfrak C[A]\to\mathsf{sSet}$, apply [lem-coef-derived-restriction-rectification] to $D=F\circ\mathfrak C[u]$. It supplies a cofibrant-fibrant $QD$, the coherent evaluation equivalence with restriction of the diagram represented by $F$, and an equivalence $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_B(QD)\to u^*U^{\mathrm{cov}}_A(F)$. These are precisely the projective and objectwise Kan hypotheses from the presentation used in step 1.

For a constant Kan diagram $X$, the projective replacement argument of step 3 and the constant-product clause of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] give the right representative $B\times X$ and the left representative $B\times X^{\mathrm{op}}$. By the Kan clause of [lem-coef-infinity-opposite-subdivision-kan-zigzag], $X^{\mathrm{op}}$ is Kan and $X$ and $X^{\mathrm{op}}$ are joined by a natural zigzag of weak homotopy equivalences between Kan complexes, so they are equivalent in the Kan-model localization. The mapping comparison of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] represents that equivalence between Kan complexes by simplicial homotopy inverse maps. Their products with $B$, and the products of their homotopies with $B$, give inverse maps up to homotopy over $B$. Thus the left representative is equivalent over $B$ to $B\times X$.

For $u:B\to A$ use [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]'s natural isomorphism $u^*U_AF\cong U_B(F\circ\mathfrak C[u]^{\mathrm{op}})$ and its covariant counterpart. Combined with step 3 this proves pullback compatibility. The isomorphisms for $u$, $v$, and $uv$ agree by that node's base-change clause. Restriction is enriched and preserves objectwise weak equivalences. The full functor-category universal property of localization in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] therefore gives its derived functor, retaining transformations and all their higher simplices. The enriched-evaluation square of step 3 commutes before localization and hence after localization. This proves compatibility on mapping spaces and with their compositions and identities; no simplicial enrichment of the chosen factorization is assumed.

Apply the contravariant version of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] and [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification] with $K=A^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\mathcal C=\mathfrak C[A]^{\mathrm{op}}$. Reversal of ordered vertex labels identifies $\mathfrak C[A^{\mathrm{op}}]$ with $\mathfrak C[A]^{\mathrm{op}}$: in every thickened simplex it reverses the labels of subsets defining the mapping objects and preserves their union composition, using the explicit thickening of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Compose the nerve of this enriched presentation with rectification to obtain the right-fibration classification. The coherent-nerve mapping comparison identifies the maps-over-$A$ mapping complexes of this locally Kan presentation with its mapping spaces. The functor-equivalence mapping-space clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] then gives the right-handed displayed formula. In degree $n$ the composition is $(g,f)(z,t)=g(f(z,t),t)$, so its coherence is the enriched composition coherence of the coherent-nerve node. For constants use the presentation's map $A\times X\to U_A(\mathrm{const}\,X)$ and its fiberwise-equivalence criterion. For pullbacks use its natural isomorphism $u^*U_AF\cong U_B(F\circ\mathfrak C[u]^{\mathrm{op}})$; replacing the restricted diagram by $QD\to D$ as in step 3 makes it cofibrant-fibrant without changing its unstraightening. Its composition law and the localization universal property used in step 5 give compatibility on full mapping spaces. No identification of a simplicial mapping complex with its opposite is asserted.

Apply [lem-coef-space-universe-repletion] to the inclusion of $\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$ into the full replete subcategory of $\mathcal V$-small Kan complexes equivalent to small ones. It gives the coherent-nerve equivalence $i:\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}\simeq\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}^{\mathrm{ess}\mathcal U}$. Postcomposition with $i$ and a quasi-inverse identifies their diagram infinity categories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus].

source.place: Universe-relative diagrams and unstraightening; full subcategory restriction

proof.text: Continue with the full replete subcategory and its inclusion $i$ from step 7. A diagram into $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ with essentially $\mathcal U$-small vertex values factors through this full subcategory: each simplex lies in it because all its vertices do. The same is true of transformations, so the factorization is full. Using the fiber clause, step 1 now restricts to exactly the left fibrations with essentially $\mathcal U$-small fibers; step 6 gives the right-fibration assertion. This restriction does not assume that $\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$ is replete in the larger functor category. If $A$ is $\mathcal U$-small, perform the construction and replacement in $\mathcal U$; the size clause of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] gives a $\mathcal U$-small total space. For a merely $\mathcal U'$-small base, work in a containing universe and use the functor equivalence of step 7.

source.place: Universe-relative diagrams and unstraightening; full subcategory restriction

proof.text: Form the explicit left fibration $\lambda:\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal E)\to\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal E$ of [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration]. Its fiber at $(x,y)$ is equivalent to the mapping space from $x$ to $y$. To see this, take opposites of that node's target-fixed slice equivalence over $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ and use [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers] to obtain equivalences on vertex fibers. The natural all-Kan zigzag of weak homotopy equivalences of [lem-coef-infinity-opposite-subdivision-kan-zigzag] identifies each opposite fiber, a Kan complex, with the original fiber in the Kan localization. The slice-fiber assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] identifies the other fiber with the right-pinched mapping space. Local $\mathcal U$-smallness consequently makes the fibers essentially $\mathcal U$-small. Steps 1 and 8 classify $\lambda$ by a coherent $H_{\mathcal E}:\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal E\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$. This constructs the functor rather than assuming that pairwise mapping spaces already form one.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 8.1.1.11 (03JQ), Proposition 8.1.2.10 (03K0) and its dual

proof.text: For fixed $e$, the slice comparisons of [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration] identify the restrictions of the twisted-arrow left fibration with $(\mathcal E_{/e})^{\mathrm{op}}$ over $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\mathcal E_{e/}$ over $\mathcal E$. The existing equivalence [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence] identifies the join slice with the fixed-target arrow model over $\mathcal E$, via its explicit map $\rho_n$ and its equation over the base. The target-arrow projection is a right fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-target-right-fibration], and the source-arrow statement is its opposite. The definition $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_{\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}}F=(U_{\mathcal E}F)^{\mathrm{op}}$ in [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] explicitly identifies covariant classification over $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ with contravariant classification over $\mathcal E$. Thus the classification from steps 1, 6 and 9 identifies the target-fixed restriction with $\mathcal E_{/e}\to\mathcal E$ classified by $H_{\mathcal E}(-,e)$ and the source-fixed restriction with $\mathcal E_{e/}\to\mathcal E$ classified by $H_{\mathcal E}(e,-)$. The formulas commute with simplicial functors and carry the degenerate identity edge to itself. These are equivalences of fibrations, not equality on their simplices.

Choose a locally Kan simplicial category $\mathcal A$ and a coherent equivalence $j:\mathcal E\simeq N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathcal A$ by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Its enriched Hom functor acts by the simplicial composition map $(u,a,v)\mapsto v\circ a\circ u$. By [lem-coef-enriched-hom-twisted-arrow-comparison], the coherent nerve of this Hom functor is represented by the twisted-arrow coupling of $N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathcal A$, with its identity witness. With precisely the explicit unstraightening and enriched-evaluation normalization used in step 1, the universal-left-fibration statement [lem-coef-universal-left-fibration-identity] says that the universal left fibration over $\mathcal S$ is the unstraightening of the identity, so pulling it back along this Hom functor is classified by that Hom functor. The functorial twisted-arrow construction gives $\operatorname{Tw}(j)$. By [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-equivalence-invariance], this is an equivalence of left fibrations over the induced product map, with the stated mapping-space maps on fibers. It compares the twisted-arrow coupling with the pullback of this universal fibration to $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal E$. The pointwise equivalence criterion and functor-equivalence mapping-space comparison from [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], together with the fiberwise criterion in [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation], make this comparison an equivalence of left fibrations. Classification and pullback compatibility identify $H_{\mathcal E}$ with the pulled-back enriched Hom functor.

source.place: Kerodon Construction 8.3.6.1 (03N6), Proposition 8.3.6.2 (03N7), Proposition 8.3.5.5 (03NK); HTT Section 3.3.2, Corollaries 3.3.2.7–8 for the independent universal identity theorem

proof.text: Under the identification with the pulled-back enriched Hom functor established in step 11, in degree $n$, precomposition and postcomposition apply simplicial composition to an $n$-simplex of its mapping complex; faces and degeneracies commute because composition is simplicial. Enriched associativity and both unit identities give their coherent homotopies under the coherent-nerve comparison. Hence $v:e\to e'$ acts at $x$ by $a\mapsto v\circ a$ on the entire space, with all higher simplices and the unit witness. This also supplies coherent dependence on $e$ for the restrictions of step 10.
